How publishers succeed with direct mail for fundraising

by AdministratorSeptember 25, 2026September 25, 2026

Share this:

  • Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn

Overview:

Direct mail can significantly boost year-end fundraising, particularly when combined with audience data, digital engagement, and a coordinated multi-channel approach. BlueLena shares insights from two years of supporting publishers in this area.

Year-end fundraising is a critical time for news publishers, and while email and onsite conversions remain the primary focus, publishers are now leveraging CRM data, donor propensity modeling, and audience segmentation to improve timing, targeting, and personalization.

Direct mail should be incorporated into this strategy.

At BlueLena’s recent end-of-year planning workshop, we shared insights from two years of assisting publishers with direct mail fundraising. Topics included audience identification, maximizing ROI, measuring results, and integrating physical mail with digital fundraising.

What we’ve learned from two years of direct mail

Results from BlueLena publishers demonstrate that direct mail is more than just an offline fundraising method.

  • In the 2025 end-of-year campaigns, the median check contribution was $100, compared to $75 for one-time online gifts. While 2.8% of direct mail recipients converted through directly attributable channels, nearly 9% converted overall during the campaign.
  • Notably, 10 of the 12 end-of-year direct mail campaigns supported by BlueLena achieved a positive return on investment based solely on directly attributable revenue.

It is important to distinguish between direct and overall conversion. For example, a reader may receive a letter, see a fundraising email, and later donate through the publisher’s website. Measuring only QR code scans or returned checks underestimates the impact of direct mail.

Direct mail is most effective when included in a comprehensive fundraising campaign rather than used in isolation.

Begin with the appropriate audience.

Effective direct mail targets the right audience rather than focusing solely on volume.

Publishers should start with their most engaged audience members—those already familiar with and appreciative of their journalism. This group includes former donors, LYBUNTs, lapsed donors, recent contributors, and highly engaged readers who have not yet donated.

Email engagement and website activity help identify promising non-donor prospects. Propensity scores, email opens, clicks, page views, and BlueDepth demographic data further refine targeting. Purchased lists are best used for top-of-funnel acquisition rather than direct fundraising appeals.

Precision is more valuable than volume; mailing to a smaller, highly qualified audience is often more effective than sending to thousands simply because their addresses are available.

When deciding between letters and postcards, select the format that aligns with your campaign objectives.

BlueLena supports both letters and postcards, each serving different purposes.

For fundraising, letters offer a key advantage by facilitating offline giving. BlueLena’s letter format includes a perforated remittance section and a reply envelope, making it easy for supporters to donate by check.

Postcards are effective for raising awareness, making announcements, or top-of-funnel acquisition. Their lower cost makes them suitable for campaigns focused on driving website visits rather than collecting checks.

Regardless of format, ensure recipients have multiple ways to respond.

Five ways to maximize direct-mail ROI

Experience indicates publishers should incorporate five key practices into their campaigns.

1. Target mailings to past donors, highly engaged non-donors, and other likely responders, rather than sending to your entire database.

2. Make it easy to give by check. Include a letter with a perforated remittance form and a reply envelope to remove barriers for donors who prefer offline giving.

3. Provide a digital path, too. Include a QR code and a simple campaign-specific URL so readers can immediately donate online.

4. Coordinate all communication channels and use a consistent fundraising message across direct mail, email, and other campaign touchpoints.

5. Control your costs. Take advantage of nonprofit postage rates when eligible and use targeting and personalization to increase the potential value of every piece mailed. Nonprofit permit approval can take two to three weeks, so publishers should plan accordingly.

Make direct mail measurable.

Many believe direct mail is difficult to measure. However, with the right infrastructure, publishers can assess its impact alongside digital channels.

BlueLena recommends creating a separate landing page or fundraising campaign for each mailing and tagging the recipient list in the CRM before distribution.

QR codes linked to personalized URLs (PURLs) enable tracking visits and online responses at the individual contact level. Checks and remittance slips can be entered into BlueLena CRM to include offline gifts in campaign reports.

However, do not limit your analysis to direct attribution alone.

Publishers should also track how many recipients donate through each channel during the campaign, as this comprehensive view demonstrates the incremental value direct mail brings to a multi-channel campaign.

Personalization matters

The principles that make personalized email effective also apply to physical mail.

Industry research presented at the workshop showed that 67% of respondents reacted to personalization, and 42% cited brand familiarity as a factor. This underscores the importance of personalization and engaging readers who already have a relationship with the organization.

This may include addressing recipients by name, acknowledging their donor status, referencing their giving history, or tailoring the appeal based on the existing relationship.

Direct mail doesn’t have to seem like junk mail.

Direct mail can have a strong personal impact when informed by accurate data.

Do not wait until November to begin.

Effective year-end mailings require careful preparation.

Publishers should first set campaign objectives, define target audiences, and decide whether to include postal addresses in audience records. Organizations seeking discounted postage should allow sufficient time for permit approval.

In October, finalize copy, creative elements, format, and donation response procedures. Production and mailing should occur in November. Evaluate results during November and December as part of the broader year-end campaign.

Consider automating direct mail year-round, not only at year-end.

An important opportunity exists after the traditional year-end campaign.

Direct mail can serve as another channel in a publisher’s lifecycle marketing strategy.

Rather than sending thousands of identical items, publishers can send individual letters or postcards when a reader meets specific criteria or reaches a significant milestone with the publication.

That could include:

  • completing a welcome series
  • abandoning a subscription or donation
  • becoming a LYBUNT or lapsed donor
  • qualifying for donor or subscriber reacquisition, or
  • reaching a point where sending a physical thank-you would strengthen the relationship

Direct mail can use the same names, donor histories, and contact information that publishers already use for personalized email. This makes direct mail a key element of the audience journey.

Bringing physical and digital fundraising together

By integrating CRM data, audience engagement, BlueDepth propensity scoring, email automation, and direct mail, publishers can identify their best prospects, communicate across multiple channels, and measure results more effectively.

For independent news organizations, a well-timed, highly personalized touchpoint can make a significant difference during the busiest fundraising season.

If you are interested in adding direct mail to your year-end fundraising strategy, contact your Publisher Success Manager to begin developing an audience, campaign, and execution plan.

About BlueLena

BlueLena is the journalism industry’s leading strategy consulting, audience and revenue development solution provider, helping more than 300 independent news organizations across North America build sustainable business models.

Founded in 2020 by publishers, journalists, and media technology professionals, BlueLena combines purpose-built technology with embedded strategic consulting and execution support to help publishers grow audiences, strengthen reader relationships, and diversify revenue through subscriptions, memberships, donations, advertising, sponsorships, and major gifts.

Its integrated platform includes audience engagement tools, CRM and moves management, donor intelligence, marketing automation, and analytics, enabling news organizations of all sizes to operate with the capabilities of a much larger organization while remaining focused on serving their communities.
